data.title: Triple combination cream (Fluocinolone + Hydroquinone + Tretinoin)
data.summary: VIII Pigmentary / depigmenting · Fixed combination: tyrosinase inhibitor + retinoid + low-potency steroid (modified Kligman formula)
data.body:
_Topicals · VIII Pigmentary / depigmenting_

**Class:** Fixed combination: tyrosinase inhibitor + retinoid + low-potency steroid (modified Kligman formula)

## Mechanism of action
- Hydroquinone 4%: inhibits tyrosinase
- Tretinoin 0.05%: increases keratinocyte turnover (removes pigment), helps hydroquinone penetrate, prevents hydroquinone oxidation
- Fluocinolone acetonide 0.01%: reduces irritation from the other two and has an anti-melanogenic effect (reduces cell metabolism)
- Original Kligman–Willis formula (1975): hydroquinone 5% + tretinoin 0.1% + dexamethasone 0.1%

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Moderate–severe melasma — short-term (approved for up to 8 weeks)
- Also listed under 'steroid combinations' in the exam list

## Dose & formulations
- Once nightly, pea-sized amount to pigmented areas, for up to 8 weeks, with strict daytime sunscreen
- Then switch to maintenance: twice-weekly TCC or non-steroid depigmenting agents (azelaic, kojic acid, niacinamide)

## Adverse effects
- Irritation, erythema, peeling, burning
- Steroid side effects with long-term use: atrophy, telangiectasia, rosacea-like eruption, acne, topical steroid dependence/TSDF — a common problem in India because of OTC misuse as 'fairness cream'
- Hydroquinone: exogenous ochronosis, confetti hypopigmentation

## Contraindications
- Pregnancy and breastfeeding
- Long-term (more than 8 weeks continuous) or whole-face use as a fairness cream
- Rosacea, acne, perioral dermatitis, broken skin

## Pregnancy & lactation
Contraindicated (tretinoin, hydroquinone).

## Viva points
- Kligman's original vs modified triple combination — know both
- Limit to 8 weeks; maintenance with non-steroid agents
- Steroid misuse in fairness creams → topical steroid-damaged face (TSDF)

_Sources: Khopkar ch.26 (Demelanizing agents); Wolverton 4e ch.45 (steroid misuse) and ch.46. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
